reader.requirement: At 85, when no GR9 overflow condition is encountered during the transfer, ON OVERFLOW is ignored and control goes to imperative-statement-2 when NOT ON OVERFLOW is written (every statement of it runs, an explicit transfer of control in it is honoured) and otherwise to the end of the STRING; the 1985 format admits ON OVERFLOW only before NOT ON OVERFLOW.

edition-consulted.switches: conditional-phrases-any-order-2002: below 2002 a NOT ON OVERFLOW written before ON OVERFLOW is refused COBOL0900
the phrase-association predicate filters formats by ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable; STRING's Pair(Overflow) row carries no construct, so every edition takes one arm

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior over StringEmitter.cs, CobolStringOps.cs, FigurativeConstants.cs: no hits; EcEmitter.EmitOverflow is gated by >>TURN enablement only (no >>TURN at 85).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: only phrase order; at 85 NOT ON OVERFLOW before ON OVERFLOW is refused (COBOL0900), at 2023 it is accepted and runs; the run-time dispatch is the same code

reader.notes: The kernel latches the overflow flag per character move and the emitter dispatches ON/NOT ON per the flag after the pointer store; ON OVERFLOW is ignored on the no-overflow path. Diagnostics cite 2023 clause numbers but the behaviour matches the 1985 text.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR9-GR10 whole (cite.py: 'OK §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR10 the text is in GR10'; 'OK §1985:VI.6.25.4 GR9 the text is in GR9'). Probes at --std 85 via run_case.py: sp1.cob (ON omitted: 'OVERFLOW'/'NOT OVERFLOW' spellings, DELIMITED without BY) printed '1 NOOVF / 1 [ABC*****]'; subp.cob NOT ON OVERFLOW sees the final pointer and receiver ('1 NOOVF 05 [ABAB****]'), ON OVERFLOW sees pointer 9 after a partial transfer ('3 OVF 09 [**ABCDEF]'); ifst.cob conditional STRING closed by ELSE and by END-IF dispatches correctly ('1 OVF','2 ELSE','3 NOOVF'); dup1/dup2.cob a second ON OVERFLOW / NOT ON OVERFLOW refused COBOL2269. Reader's zero-move NOOVF at pointer 5 of 4 follows GR9's 'Before each move of a character' literally. No counter-example found.
